description:
## Question

Does the actually installed Radicle 1.9.x command surface provide the mechanics the replacement will freeze — and where do the documentation-derived semantics, or the facts the research record flags UNCONFIRMED, diverge from installed behavior?

Part of: #538 (predecessor to every implementation unit that relies on documentation-derived command semantics).

## Time box

One focused session.

## Context

The `radicle-stock-collaboration-mechanics` research record (2026-07-10, in `.runa/workspace/`) grounds the replacement's mechanics in the official radicle.dev guides and man pages — but `rad` is installed nowhere on this host today, so every command semantic is documentation-derived. The requirements make re-verification against the installed surface an explicit predecessor: implementation must not freeze mechanics on unverified semantics.

Facts the research record flags UNCONFIRMED and this spike must resolve or explicitly bound:

- the non-delegate permission matrix for issue assignment and labeling (decides whether claiming is DID assignment or the documented comment convention);
- ssh-agent signing behavior in practice on the verification environment;
- external-COB validation semantics (context only — custom COBs are out of scope this phase);
- concurrent multi-node single-host operation;
- whether any HTTP write endpoint exists (expected: none — read-only daemon).

The verification environment is a bounded scratch setup (rad toolchain plus scratch repository/identities); the production identity and node topology are other units' work.

## Expected output

- [ ] Written findings recorded durably: the research record artifact updated (or a successor research record delivered) and a findings comment on this issue.
- [ ] Per mechanic class — identity/auth, issue lifecycle (open/show/comment/assign/label/state), patch lifecycle (magic-ref submission, push options, revision publication), review (revision addressing, accept/reject), merge and canonical publication, sync/replication read-back — a confirmed/diverged verdict against the research record's documented semantics, with the installed version pinned.
- [ ] Each UNCONFIRMED fact above resolved, or explicitly recorded as still-unconfirmed with the fallback the dependent unit must use (e.g. comment-convention claiming).
- [ ] Follow-up issues filed if any divergence rescopes a dependent unit.

## Dependencies

None in-graph. Requires a rad 1.9.x toolchain installable in a bounded environment. Deliberately not gated on tesserine/commons#108: this is knowledge acquisition, not implementation of the replacement.
title: spike: verify the installed Radicle command surface against the documented mechanics
